title: Mosiah Grants Permission to Inquire
summary: After three years of continual peace, Mosiah wants to know about the people who went to Lehi-Nephi. His people have heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and weary him with their teasings. Mosiah grants permission for sixteen strong men to go and inquire about their brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah had had continual peace for three years.
He wanted to know about the people who went to dwell in the land or city of Lehi-Nephi.
His people had heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and wearied him with their teasings.
Mosiah granted that sixteen of their strong men might go to Lehi-Nephi to inquire about their brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown with unnamed members of his people as they weary him with their teasings.
unspecified_visual_details: The present setting, appearances, clothing, and architecture are not specified.

narration.text: his people had heard nothing from them from the time they left the land of Zarahemla; therefore, they wearied him with their teasings.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses grant permission for the journey; they do not narrate the men's departure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the sixteen men setting out or arriving in Lehi-Nephi.
Do not identify Mosiah's people by an unsupplied group name or invent their words.
Do not depict the people in Lehi-Nephi as present with Mosiah.

title: Setting Out and Wandering
summary: On the morrow, they start to go up with Ammon as their leader. Not knowing the course to the land of Lehi-Nephi, they wander in the wilderness for forty days.

explicit_facts.text: They start to go up on the morrow, with Ammon among them.
Ammon is a strong and mighty man, a descendant of Zarahemla, and their leader.
They do not know the course to the land of Lehi-Nephi and wander in the wilderness for forty days.

unspecified_visual_details: The number and identities of the other travelers.

narration.text: And now, they knew not the course they should travel in the wilderness to go up to the land of Lehi-Nephi; therefore they wandered many days in the wilderness, even forty days did they wander.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not assume they entered the wilderness on the day they started to go up.
prohibited_inventions: Do not specify a number of travelers or add a route, obstacle, or incident during the forty days.

title: Camp at the Hill
summary: After forty days, the group reaches a hill north of Shilom and pitches tents. Ammon takes Amaleki, Helem, and Hem down into the land of Nephi.
locations: A hill north of the land of Shilom

explicit_facts.text: After wandering forty days, the group reaches a hill north of Shilom and pitches tents there.
Ammon takes three companions, Amaleki, Helem, and Hem, down into the land of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The camp at the hill and the descent toward the land of Nephi are successive drawable moments.
unspecified_visual_details: The hill's appearance, tent design, and the terrain between the hill and the land of Nephi.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the whole group going down with Ammon; only he and the three named companions are specified as going.

explicit_facts.text: They met the king of the people who were in the land of Nephi and the land of Shilom.

title: Before King Limhi
summary: After two days in prison, they are brought before the king and their bands are loosed. Limhi identifies himself, asks why they came near the city walls while he was outside the gate with his guards, and permits them to speak.
locations: An unspecified place before the king

explicit_facts.text: After two days in prison, they are brought before the king, their bands are loosed, and they are commanded to answer his questions.
Limhi identifies himself as the son of Noah and grandson of Zeniff.
Limhi asks why they came near the city walls while he was outside the gate with his guards.
Limhi says he preserved them so he could question them, and permits them to speak.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi and the people brought before him can be shown facing one another during the questioning.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the setting, clothing, and people present.

title: Limhi Rejoices After Hearing Ammon
summary: After hearing Ammon, Limhi is exceedingly glad. He says his brethren in Zarahemla are alive and that he will cause his people to rejoice the next day. He says his people are in bondage to the Lamanites and bear a grievous tax. He expects their brethren to deliver them, even if they become slaves to the Nephites instead.

Limhi says he knows his brethren in Zarahemla are alive and plans to cause his people to rejoice the next day.

Limhi expects his brethren to deliver his people and says becoming slaves to the Nephites would be better than paying tribute to the king of the Lamanites.

He recalls God bringing the children of Israel through the Red Sea and feeding them manna, and bringing their fathers out of Jerusalem.
He says God brought them into bondage because of their iniquities and abominations.

summary: Limhi recounts that the people slew a prophet who testified of their wickedness and prophesied of Christ. He says they put the prophet to death because he taught that Christ would take flesh and blood.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi says the people slew a prophet, a chosen man of God who told them of their wickedness and prophesied of Christ.
